R0203.title: DApp Frontend Hijacking
R0203.definition: Attackers hijack IPFS gateways or poison DNS to tamper with DApp frontend code, replacing payment addresses or injecting malicious interactions without user awareness.
R0203.description:
DApp frontend hijacking targets the user access layer rather than the on-chain contract. Attackers may abuse DNS, IPFS gateways, CDN configuration, or frontend dependencies to alter displayed content and wallet interaction parameters.

Users see a familiar interface while signing requests or recipient addresses may be replaced. Projects need release integrity, domain hardening, resource verification, and independent transaction previews.

Limitation: Requires control over intermediate network nodes
R0203.influence: Frontend hijacking can make users sign malicious transactions on a familiar DApp interface, sending funds or approvals to attackers.

observables: DApp front-end resource integrity hashes mismatch the official release version
Recipient addresses or contract parameters in signature requests differ from what the UI displays
Front-end code returned by IPFS gateways or CDNs shows unexpected changes
DNS resolution results point to non-official IPs in specific regions or time windows
Front-end dependency package versions are replaced with new versions containing anomalous logic
